tca.entry.text_dramatic: The ferry noses into the harbor of the cell's great wheel. You ride inside the acetyl group — two carbons cradled in coenzyme A's grip — and ahead oxaloacetate, the four-carbon socket, waits with its arms open. The handoff is quick: CoA slips away, empty, ready to ferry again, and the wheel begins to turn. This is the hub of respiration — everything the host ate has been broken down to reach this doorway. Now the wheel decides: burn, bank, or build.
tca.entry.text_teaching: Cycle entry (TCA-ENTRY-01): acetyl-CoA delivers a two-carbon acetyl group to the citric acid cycle, condensing with the four-carbon oxaloacetate to form citrate (LibreTexts 16.02 Introduction). The cycle is the hub of respiration: carbon skeletons, electron carriers, and biosynthetic building blocks all pass through it. One clarity note before the wheel turns: you are a single carbon atom — carbon-14 is the tracking label the story uses to follow you, nothing more — and you ride inside the acetyl group's two carbons. Which of those two you are is deliberately not specified: the game's shuffle (ahead) treats every carbon identically, a stated simplification. The next node shows the condensation itself.

tca.citrate_synthase.text_dramatic: The wheel's first gate. Citrate synthase swings wide — oxaloacetate locked in one jaw — and the acetyl group, your ferry, slides into the other. Then the jaws close: the enzyme wraps its catch and fuses the two in a single motion, spending the thioester bond that carried you across like a coin tossed to the ferryman. Citrate, six carbons, is born. Six carbons ride the wheel now. One of them is you. Hold onto that thought — the wheel is about to make it strange.
tca.citrate_synthase.text_teaching: Step 1 of the cycle's chemistry (TCA-CS-01): citrate synthase condenses oxaloacetate + acetyl-CoA → citrate via an (S)-citryl-CoA intermediate; ΔG°′ = −7.5 kcal/mol, driven by thioester hydrolysis (LibreTexts 16.02 §1). The enzyme uses induced fit: the active site closes only around both substrates, shielding the chemistry until the (S)-citryl-CoA intermediate forms and is hydrolyzed (the published catalytic residues — Asp375/His274/His320/Arg329 — carry pig-enzyme numbering; the cast here is a bird's). Cast (CAST-CSC-PDB-01): PDB 1CSC — citrate synthase from chicken (Gallus gallus), 1.70 Å (Karpusas, Holland, Remington 1991). Dimer note, stated for scope honesty: the structure you see is the asymmetric unit — ONE chain. The functional enzyme is a homodimer (two identical chains working together); loading the full biological assembly would need an engine enhancement that is deliberately out of this phase's scope, so the game shows one chain and says so. Stereospecificity (TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01): citrate is prochiral — its two carboxymethyl arms are chemically equivalent yet distinguishable (one pro-R, one pro-S) — and citrate synthase builds exactly one stereoisomer. That hidden handedness is about to matter. Exploration note: the edit offer at this node is honest structural exploration — citrate synthase carries no disease point mutant (UniProt O75390 annotates zero natural point variants; the ClinVar Pathogenic records are all structural variants, out of reach of a single-residue edit).

tca.aconitase.text_dramatic: Aconitase takes citrate in hand and turns it inside out. The molecule's symmetry is a disguise, and the enzyme's iron-sulfur heart sees through it: though citrate's two arms are chemical twins, aconitase always grips the same one — the arm that was here before you arrived. A proton leaves, water returns, cis-aconitate flips a full half-turn in the enzyme's grasp, and isocitrate emerges. The wheel does not care which arm you rode in on. But the enzyme does — and its choice is why your exit is postponed, not immediate. Meanwhile, in the host: one wrong letter in the aconitase recipe — S112R — and the mitochondria starve in place, taking the child's sight and balance with them.
tca.aconitase.text_teaching: Step 2 (TCA-ACONITASE-01): aconitase isomerizes citrate → isocitrate via the cis-aconitate intermediate, which undergoes a 180-degree flip around its C=C bond inside the active site; the enzyme uses an Fe₄S₄ cluster whose labile iron directly binds the substrate (ΔG°′ ≈ +1.5 kcal/mol — nearly balanced, so the step runs readily in both directions; LibreTexts 16.02 + Wikipedia 'Aconitase'). The discrimination (TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01): citrate's two carboxymethyl arms are equivalent — one pro-R, one pro-S — yet aconitase acts ONLY on the arm derived from oxaloacetate, never the acetyl-derived arm. Keep this fact: it is the mechanism behind the isotope surprise you will meet two nodes from now (your carbons' fate is deferred, not immediate). Disease story (DIS-ACO2-01-cand): ACO2 S112R is associated with infantile cerebellar-retinal degeneration (ICRD, MIM:614559); UniProt annotates S112R/G259D/K736N in ICRD and L74V/G661R in OPA9 (MIM:616289). The reverse fix, R112S, is the healthy sequence — and the restoration arc the game can replay. Cast honesty (CAST-ACO2-PDB-01-cand): the structure on screen is PDB 1ACO — BOVINE (Bos taurus) mitochondrial aconitase, 2.05 Å, trans-aconitate bound (Lauble et al. 1994). No human ACO2 crystal structure exists (UniProt Q99798 has zero PDB cross-refs), so the game casts a bovine stand-in and says so; the human↔bovine residue mapping used by the game's edits was derived by real sequence alignment, never assumed.

tca.aconitase_restored.text_dramatic: Aconitase, made whole. The wrong letter in the host's recipe is set back — the intrusive arginine yields to serine — and a healthy wild-type structure is brought alongside yours, the two shapes settling into agreement atom by atom. The iron-sulfur heart steadies. The wheel, indifferent as ever, keeps turning; it does not wait for repaired enzymes. The shuffle lies just ahead.
tca.aconitase_restored.text_teaching: This is the aconitase restoration reveal — the arc's staged replay of a corrected enzyme, honest about what is real. The mechanics you just watched are real PyMOL operations: the game applied a point mutation at residue 85 of the on-screen enzyme (setting it back to serine, SER — the bovine 1ACO position that corresponds to human ACO2's S112, a mapping derived by real sequence alignment), loaded the healthy wild-type cast — PDB 1ACO, 2.05 Å — and superimposed it onto your edited copy (alignment on C-alpha atoms, cmd.super) so the two structures can be compared. The human story it stands in for (DIS-ACO2-01-cand): ACO2 S112R is associated with infantile cerebellar-retinal degeneration (ICRD, MIM:614559); the reverse fix R112S restores the wild-type sequence the game replays here. One honesty note: the cast is the bovine enzyme — the human protein has no crystal structure — so this is a derived, near-identical stand-in (96.4% sequence identity in the aligned region), not the human molecule itself. The wheel ahead does not care: the story's carbon rides on.

tca.shuffle.text_dramatic: The great wheel does not stop for anyone. Each pass, the carbon lottery: somewhere in the cycle's symmetric stretch your carbon loses its seat number, and two doors stand open with equal odds. Behind one — the exit position, where the next decarboxylation will reach. Behind the other — another lap aboard, the fire burning, the odds reset. Spin.
tca.shuffle.text_teaching: The RNG heart of the game (TCA-RNG-WEIGHT-02-cand): every pass, the wheel-spin stands in for the cycle's one genuinely random carbon event — the 50/50 label-scrambling that happens when the hero carbon passes the symmetric succinate/fumarate intermediates, where the molecule's symmetry erases which end is which. Outcome 1, exit position: the carbon lands in an oxaloacetate carboxyl seat, positioned to leave as CO2 when the cycle next turns. Outcome 2, retained: it rides another turn — and every future pass is a fresh coin flip. The 0.5/0.5 weight is the game-design value (human-approved; the value of the earlier TCA-RNG-WEIGHT-01, unchanged), but the SEMANTICS are anchored to the real stochastic event, because the isotope chemistry demands it (TCA-CARBON-FATE-01-cand): the two CO2 released in any turn derive from the recycled oxaloacetate frame, not directly from the incoming acetyl carbons. And the prochirality mechanism (TCA-RNG-CITRATE-PROCHIRALITY-01) is why: aconitase always acts on the oxaloacetate-derived arm, so the acetyl carbons can never be the immediate ones off — their exit is deferred across turns. Two honesty notes: (1) the shuffle is deliberately hero-carbon-agnostic — the precise fate depends on which of the acetyl's two carbons you are, and the game states the simplification instead of pretending; (2) the 'cycle has spun too long' option below is a GAME-DESIGN CAP — it fires after more than five passes (N=5 is a tuned parameter, not a science claim; a real carbon's exit odds never expire).

choices.label: The wheel spins — your carbon lands in an exit position
The wheel spins — your carbon is retained aboard
The cycle has spun too long — the host fades

tca.co2_turn1.text_dramatic: Exit position. The wheel has seated your carbon where the fire's reach falls — a carboxyl chair on the oxaloacetate frame that is already forming ahead. The cycle's two exhalations wait: gates that release CO2 into the dark of the matrix. This time, the breath may carry you. Or — the wheel trading seats behind your back — the breath may carry the frame's own carbon, released while you ride on, unburned, past the very furnace that seemed to have your name. Ride another turn and trust the odds, or walk on and watch where the wheel's CO2 actually leaves.
tca.co2_turn1.text_teaching: The wheel put your carbon in an exit position (TCA-RNG-WEIGHT-02-cand, outcome 1): it now sits where the coming decarboxylations reach. But here is the isotope surprise (TCA-CARBON-FATE-01-cand): the two CO2 released in a turn of the cycle derive from OXALOACETATE carbons — the recycled four-carbon frame — NOT directly from the incoming acetyl carbons. The acetyl carbons join the oxaloacetate backbone only after the first turn, and their loss as CO2 requires several subsequent turns. So even seated in the exit position, the carbon leaving as CO2 right now may not be yours — the pool turns over as a whole (two CO2 per turn; the first decarboxylation is the next node, TCA-IDH3-01). Both doors stay honest: the loop choice rides again (the geometric tail — retained carbons simply face the same 50/50 on the next pass); the forward choice continues the story toward the wheel's actual CO2 gates.

tca.co2_turn2.text_dramatic: Retained. The wheel keeps you aboard — the scramble left your carbon in an internal seat, deep in the frame of the four-carbon acids, where the coming exhalations cannot reach. The wheel turns. The furnace breathes. Not you. Not this pass. And the wheel holds no memory: every lap from here is a fresh toss, the same two doors, the same equal odds. Ride the odds again, or walk on toward the soul's road and let the wheel decide the rest.
tca.co2_turn2.text_teaching: The wheel kept you aboard (TCA-RNG-WEIGHT-02-cand, outcome 2): the 50/50 scramble at the symmetric stretch left the hero carbon in an internal (methylene/central) position, so the coming decarboxylations cannot release it. The CO2 that does leave this pass comes from the pool's carboxyl seats — the recycled oxaloacetate frame (TCA-CARBON-FATE-01-cand; the first decarboxylation is at the next node, TCA-IDH3-01). Your carbon now rides the four-carbon acids — succinate, fumarate, malate, oxaloacetate — and every future pass through the wheel is a fresh 50/50. Two verbatim-honest footnotes from the isotope result: the acetyl carbons' full exit 'requires several turns', and because the cycle also feeds biosynthesis, a retained carbon can even be withdrawn into building material before it ever burns. The loop choice spins again; the forward choice continues the story.

tca.isocitrate_dh.text_dramatic: Isocitrate dehydrogenase strikes. The wheel's first true exhalation: a carboxyl tears free and leaves as CO2, and NADH — the ferry that will carry the harvested electrons — takes on cargo. This is one of the cycle's key regulatory steps: the point where the cell reads the wheel and tunes it. But watch what actually leaves. The carbon that flies off may not be one of the two that arrived with you. The wheel has been trading seats behind your back — and yours, when it comes due, comes due later.
tca.isocitrate_dh.text_teaching: Step 3 (TCA-IDH3-01): isocitrate dehydrogenase — the NAD⁺-dependent, mitochondrial form (IDH3, an α₂βγ assembly with the catalytic site on the α subunit, activated by citrate and ADP) — oxidatively decarboxylates isocitrate → α-ketoglutarate + CO₂ + NADH; a key regulatory step of the cycle (ΔG°′ ≈ −2.0 kcal/mol; LibreTexts 16.02). Wording discipline: some tables call this the cycle's pace-setting step, but the stronger claim rests on a regulation source this game has not yet verified — so the game states only the verified form, a key regulatory step. THE ISOTOPE-SURPRISE BEAT (TCA-CARBON-FATE-01-cand): the CO2 leaving here derives from an oxaloacetate carbon — the recycled frame — not directly from the acetyl carbons you arrived with; if you are still aboard after the shuffle, this exhalation is probably not yours. Cast (CAST-IDH3-PDB-01-cand): PDB 5GRE — the wild-type human IDH3 α-γ heterodimer with Mg²⁺, citrate and ADP bound, 2.65 Å (the citrate/ADP-regulated form). The game casts only wild-type enzyme structures: an earlier candidate for this slot carried a crystallization mutation in the regulatory γ subunit and was replaced after verification. Numbering bridge (derived by sequence alignment, 100% identity in aligned pairs): human M204 sits at 5GRE chain-A residue 177 — PDB numbering runs UniProt − 27, the construct dropping the N-terminal 27 residues. Disease story (DIS-IDH3A-01-cand): IDH3A M204I is classified Pathogenic in ClinVar (VCV000977473) and associated with RP90 (retinitis pigmentosa); UniProt P50213 annotates 8 RP90 missense variants including M204I and R316C (the alternate confirmed-pathogenic allele, VCV000977472); UniProt's 'uncertain significance' label for the set is stale. The reverse fix (I204M) restores the wild-type methionine.

choices.label: Examine the isocitrate dehydrogenase active site

tca.akg_dh.text_dramatic: Alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase strikes next — twin to the ferryman who delivered you, wearing the same three-part machinery. A second carboxyl tears free and leaves as CO2; another NADH loads; and the enzyme forges a thioester bond, high-energy cargo the wheel will spend two steps from now. By the old textbook tally, both carbons that arrived with you would be gone by now. The wheel knows better. Look at what is actually leaving: still the recycled frame's carbons. Your exit-debt stands open — and the wheel always collects, given turns enough.
tca.akg_dh.text_teaching: Step 4 (TCA-OGDH-01): α-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase oxidatively decarboxylates α-KG → succinyl-CoA + CO₂ + NADH (ΔG°′ ≈ −7.2 kcal/mol). The complex is mechanistically homologous to the pyruvate dehydrogenase you met at the doorway: same E1/E2/E3 architecture, same TPP/lipoamide/FAD cofactors (LibreTexts 16.02, cross-referencing 16.1). Isotope-surprise, again (TCA-CARBON-FATE-01-cand): this is the turn's second CO2, and it too derives from the oxaloacetate frame — the textbook shorthand that 'both acetyl carbons are released by this step' is precisely what the isotope-labeling result overturned. Your carbons joined the oxaloacetate backbone after the first turn and leave only over several subsequent turns. Disease story, now explorable (DIS-OGDH-01-cand): OGDH P189L is associated with oxoglutarate dehydrogenase deficiency (OGDHD; OMIM 613022.0003 / phenotype 203740), classified Pathogenic in ClinVar (VCV002443831); it was found homozygous in an Ashkenazi-Jewish patient, and HEK293 expression shows an unstable protein (Whittle et al. 2023, PMID 36520152). Evidence-tier caveat, kept honest: this ClinVar record rests on a single submitter with no assertion criteria provided, literature-only — a weaker tier than, say, the fumarase story two nodes ahead (multi-submitter with functional annotation). A confirmed pathogenic mutation, with that provenance stated. The reverse fix (L189P) restores proline at UniProt residue 189 — no PDB mapping needed: this node loads no structure (narrative-only), so UniProt numbering is authoritative, and the game's edit here is a staged exploration, not an on-structure correction.

tca.succinyl_coa_synthetase.text_dramatic: Succinyl-CoA is a wound spring. Succinyl-CoA synthetase lets it unwind — succinate at last, a symmetric four-carbon — and catches the released energy as GTP: the only coin the wheel mints directly; every other step pays in electrons. A phosphate hops from CoA to GDP by way of a histidine relay at the enzyme's heart, and somewhere soon that GTP will trade itself for the cell's common currency. The wheel rolls the four symmetric carbons onward, into the stretch where positions lose their names.
tca.succinyl_coa_synthetase.text_teaching: Step 5 (TCA-SCS-01): succinyl-CoA synthetase converts succinyl-CoA → succinate, coupling thioester-bond cleavage to GTP synthesis — the cycle's ONLY substrate-level phosphorylation (ΔG°′ ≈ −0.8 kcal/mol; LibreTexts 16.02). The mechanism threads the phosphate through a phosphohistidine intermediate (His246 in the E. coli enzyme — numbering caveat; the mammalian relay is homologous). Nucleoside-diphosphate kinase then trades GTP ⇄ ATP, folding this coin into the cell's common currency; mammals carry both GDP-forming and ADP-forming isoforms. No cast loads here (narrative-only node; the registered human SUCLG1 structure record, PDB 6WCV, stays dormant — no reveal mechanics exist on this node). Disease story (DIS-SUCLG1-01-cand): SUCLG1 G85A (rs267607097) is associated with MTDPS9, a mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome (OMIM 245400); UniProt annotates M14L, G37A (no disease note), G85A (MTDPS9, rs267607097) and P170R (MTDPS9, rs267607099). The reverse fix (A85G) restores glycine — the game's known-edit here is a staged exploration (no on-structure correction; this node loads no structure).

choices.label: Examine the succinyl-CoA synthetase active site

tca.fumarase.text_dramatic: Water crosses the double bond in one stereospecific stroke: fumarase builds only one of the two possible malates — the L-form, the only one the wheel accepts. Fumarate becomes malate. Notice where you are. This stretch of the wheel is symmetric: four carbons in a line, no memory of which end is which. When the wheel passes through here, seat numbers dissolve. Somewhere in this symmetry hides the honest coin flip the game has been dramatizing since the shuffle. And in the host, fumarase carries a darker story: one wrong letter — R233H — and the enzyme is struck from both of its jobs, feeding the wheel and guarding the DNA.
tca.fumarase.text_teaching: Step 6 (TCA-FH-01): fumarase (fumarate hydratase) reversibly hydrates fumarate → L-malate — a stereospecific trans-addition of water across the double bond (ΔG°′ ≈ −0.9 kcal/mol; class-II enzyme; LibreTexts 16.02). Symmetry note: succinate and fumarate are symmetric molecules — this stretch is where the isotope label genuinely scrambles, the physical 50/50 that the shuffle node dramatizes (TCA-RNG-WEIGHT-02-cand). No cast loads here (narrative-only node; the registered human fumarate hydratase structure, PDB 5UPP, 1.8 Å, stays dormant). Disease story (DIS-FH-01-cand): FH R233H (rs121913123 — an earlier game record carried rs121913121, which belongs to a different variant, N107T; corrected) is associated with HLRCC (hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal-cell cancer; OMIM 150800); UniProt annotates it 'catalytically inactive mutant; abolished ability to promote DNA repair'. This is the strongest evidence tier in the TCA disease set — multi-submitter ClinVar Pathogenic plus an explicit functional annotation. The reverse fix (H233R) restores histidine.

tca.malate_dh.text_dramatic: Malate dehydrogenase closes the circle. Malate gives up two electrons and a proton to NAD⁺ — the third electron-cargo of the turn — and becomes oxaloacetate: the empty socket the wheel began with. By the cold arithmetic of energy this step runs uphill, and the wheel drives it anyway, because the next condensation downstream pulls the product away the instant it forms. The cycle is whole again. Ahead: the wheel — or the door to the two good fates, where a carbon can be withdrawn, alive, before it ever burns.
tca.malate_dh.text_teaching: Step 7 (TCA-MDH2-01): malate dehydrogenase oxidizes L-malate → oxaloacetate + NADH — ΔG°′ = +7.1 kcal/mol, UNFAVORABLE on its own, pulled forward because citrate synthase consumes the product the moment it appears (the textbook coupling example); the step regenerates the cycle's OAA acceptor and banks the turn's third NADH (LibreTexts 16.02). Isoforms: MDH1 works the cytosol; MDH2 — this story's enzyme — the mitochondrial matrix. Cast (CAST-MDH2-PDB-01-cand): PDB 4WLU — human MDH2 with L-malate and NAD⁺ bound at the active site, 2.14 Å (LibreTexts' own teaching model — substrate and cofactor visible where the chemistry happens). Numbering check (verified against the fetched coordinates): 4WLU residue 37 is glycine in every chain — the UniProt G37 numbering and the PDB numbering align directly, so the game's residue-37 edit story maps cleanly onto the cast. Disease story (DIS-MDH2-01-cand): MDH2 G37R is associated with DEE51 (developmental and epileptic encephalopathy 51; OMIM 617339); UniProt annotates 'severe defects in aerobic respiration... when assayed in a heterologous system' (P133L and P207L are also DEE51 alleles). The reverse fix (R37G) restores glycine.

tca.divert_to_good.text_dramatic: The wheel turns, and turn it will — but a wheel is not a prison. Here the road forks. Follow the soul: let your electrons ride the convoys to the electron-transport chain, where the host harvests them into ATP — and your carbon body, spent, is breathed out as CO2. Or divert: step off the wheel while you are still matter, still carbon, still buildable — withdrawn into the cell's own construction, a fatty-acid store or an amino-acid brick. The amphibolic truth of this cycle is that burning and building share the same wheel. Choose which passenger you will be.
tca.divert_to_good.text_teaching: The branch point (TCA-AMPHIBOLIC-01): the citric acid cycle is amphibolic — it serves both breakdown and biosynthesis. Its intermediates are withdrawn (cataplerotic) for building: citrate for lipid synthesis, oxaloacetate and α-KG for amino-acid synthesis (Wikipedia 'Citric acid cycle' + LibreTexts 16.02 Summary / 16.04). Anti-confusion, stated plainly: the two roads separate the hero's two natures. The ETC road follows the SOUL — the electrons your atom banked into NADH travel the transport chain toward ATP, while the carbon body itself is eventually shed as CO2. The divert roads keep the CARBON BODY: an intermediate is withdrawn from the cycle pre-oxidation, so your carbon lives on as stored fat or as an amino-acid building block. Neither road turns carbon into ATP — the electrons, not the carbon, are what the ETC harvests. The two good exits ahead carry the details.

choices.label: Follow the soul to the ETC
Divert to fatty-acid storage (your carbon body lives on)
Divert to amino-acid synthesis (become a building block)
